lens: Performance and architecture reviewer owning the retained native board view (modules/arrows-board Kotlin + Swift, BoardView.tsx, StaticBoardSurface.native.tsx, exitAnimationConfig.ts). Everything below was read from the source in this checkout, not from the plan's description of it. Register is marked per claim: EXECUTED = I ran it; READ = I read the file and am quoting it; INFERRED = reasoning on top of those.
strongest_case_the_plan_is_wrong:
The plan treats reduce-motion as a defect confined to the Reanimated feedback layer ("27 withTiming call sites", "six withTiming configs"). It is not. `reducedMotion` is a FIELD OF THE NATIVE EXIT PROTOCOL — src/ui/nativeExitAnimation.ts serializes it as header token 3, and both native renderers branch on it in their draw path: ArrowsBoardView.kt drawExitSlot does `val travelled = if (slot.reducedMotion) 0f else progress*progress*totalLength` and swaps the smoothstep fade for a linear `1f - progress`; ArrowsBoardView.swift:168/177/191-193 mirrors it (`phase.toValue = reducedMotion ? patternSum : patternSum - totalLength`, `translation.toValue = reducedMotion ? ...`, `opacity.keyTimes = reducedMotion ? [0,1] : [0,0.55,1]`). [READ]

Two consequences the plan never states. (1) The reduce-motion census is incomplete at its boundary: under OS reduce motion the shipped exit is a STATIONARY dash that fades linearly in place, and the arrowhead does not translate. Nobody wrote that down, nobody signed off on it, and W0-03's "the player sees exactly two magenta arrows" and W2-02's "27 call sites" both describe a world where the exit is untouched. (2) More damaging: the harness forces `animator_duration_scale 0` (benchmark.mjs:353 [EXECUTED grep]), which per this project's own memory flips `useReducedMotion()` to true; BoardView passes that value straight into `setNativeExitAnimation({... reducedMotion ...})` [READ]. Therefore EVERY `exit` phase number this project has ever recorded — including the 21.0/23.2/29.5/36.1/36.8 ms column in docs/perf-tap-forgiveness-ab-2026-09-08.md — measured a dash that does not move, with a different fade curve, on a code path no non-reduce-motion player ever sees. [INFERRED from those two reads plus the project's established memory that scale 0 flips useReducedMotion]

The plan then builds its whole verification apparatus (W2-01 capture mode, W6-11 --motion-scale, W6-12 pixel floor, W6-13 --assert-rendered) on the premise that restoring the scale to 1 recovers "the shipped experience" for comparison against history. It does the opposite: it flips the native exit into its real form for the first time, so the first honest exit measurement will have NO comparable HEAD baseline. W2-08, W2-09, W2-12, W3-09 and W5-12 all quote or compare exit-phase behaviour and all inherit this. That is the single largest unacknowledged premise failure in the plan.

Self-attack: the weak link is "scale 0 sets _REANIMATED_IS_REDUCED_MOTION". I could not grep it (the Android source is prebuilt in this checkout), so that one hop is INFERRED — but it is the project's own recorded fact, already blamed for invalidating an accepted result, and the plan asserts it in five separate steps. What I add on top of it is read directly from Kotlin and Swift. The objection survives.

Second self-attack, on my scrim objection (W2-04): a fair counter is that Reanimated resumes a stalled animation when the app returns to foreground, so the callback fires late rather than never, and the app is not bricked. That counter largely wins, so I downgrade the claim from "unplayable" to "stalls with no backstop" — but it does not rescue the design, because the plan's own W0-02 establishes that in this codebase a visibility-critical property reachable only from an animation completion callback is a defect class, and W2-06 requires a background-during-entrance test for the panel while W2-04 — which gates loadLevel itself — requires none.

kills.reason: Three defects. (1) SCOPE IS WRONG AT ITS BOUNDARY: the step enumerates 'all 27 withTiming/withSpring/withRepeat/withDelay call sites' and misses the reduce-motion branch that lives in Kotlin and Swift. ArrowsBoardView.kt drawExitSlot sets travelled=0 and a linear fade when the payload's reducedMotion flag is 1; Swift:168/177/191-193 mirrors it. [READ] A source-text lint over src/ can never see it, so the step's own regression guard certifies a census it did not take. (2) The proposed jest source-scan lists withTiming/withSpring/withRepeat but not withDecay — BoardView.tsx imports and uses withDecay for pan momentum and it also takes a reduceMotion key. [READ] (3) The acceptance criterion 'With OS reduce motion OFF, W2-01 captures of the same three effects are frame-for-frame unchanged from HEAD' is unreachable: adb screenrecord frames are not phase-locked to the app across two builds and two launches, so frame-for-frame identity is not a property that can hold. This is the invented-unreachable-target pattern.
kills.replacement: Split into (a) a policy pass over the JS call sites including withDecay, (b) an explicit written decision on what the NATIVE exit renders under reduce motion — the current behaviour (stationary fading dash, head does not translate) is defensible but must be recorded in DESIGN.md and signed off, not discovered, and (c) replace the frame-for-frame criterion with a bounded one: the effect's visible duration in recorded frames is within +/-2 frames of HEAD at the same recorder frame rate, plus a stated first/last-frame appearance check. Merge with W0-03 (see below) so one change ships once.

kills.reason: The fix is right; two of its stated premises are not, and it duplicates W2-02. (1) FALSE PREMISE: 'This removes the split-brain where the JS useReducedMotion() value and Reanimated's UI-thread isReduceMotionOnUI could disagree.' At the pinned 4.5.1 they cannot disagree. node_modules/react-native-reanimated/src/ReducedMotion.ts computes `const IS_REDUCED_MOTION_ENABLED_IN_SYSTEM = isReducedMotionEnabledInSystem()` once at module init and seeds BOTH jsValue and uiValue.value from that same constant; they only diverge if setEnabled() is called, and nothing in src/ calls it. [EXECUTED: cat of ReducedMotion.ts] The extra threading work is justified by a hazard that does not exist at this version. (2) INCOMPLETE: it enumerates six withTiming sites as the whole defect and never mentions that the exit slither also degrades under the same flag, in native code. (3) DUPLICATE: W0-03 and W2-02 are the same edit to the same six lines with contradictory scopes and contradictory acceptance — whichever ships second will find its 'On HEAD the same capture contains zero such frames' pre-fix criterion already false. The verified-correct parts: blockerOpacityAt(1)=0 exactly (t>=0.4, f=1, 1-1*(3-2)=0) and the ShakingArrow colour resolves to pure ink at k=1 (eased=1-(1-1)^2=1). [EXECUTED: read feedbackCurves.ts and StaticBoardSurface.native.tsx:315-318]
kills.replacement: Keep the ReduceMotion.Never + own-the-degradation fix and the curve extraction. Delete the split-brain justification and replace it with the true one: the render code, not Reanimated, should decide what degrades, because the curves are shared with the web SVG layer and with a native path Reanimated does not control. Fold W2-02 into this step and ship the reduce-motion policy exactly once, including the native exit decision.

kills.reason: The `--assert-rendered` gate is validated by exactly one pair (blocked at scale 1 passes / scale 0 fails) and the step declares that pair 'the whole verification'. That pair does not generalise to the phase the gate will actually be used on. Run it against `exit` at scale 0 and it PASSES while nothing moves: drawExitSlot with reducedMotion=true still redraws the dash every frame with a decreasing alpha (`1f - progress`) and still calls postInvalidateOnAnimation, so the changed-pixel fraction is large and the floor is cleared — by a fade, not by motion. [READ ArrowsBoardView.kt drawExitSlot] A gate that reports 'the effect rendered' for a frozen slither is worse than no gate, because W2-08, W2-09 and W5-12 are all exit-phase steps that would cite it. Second problem: the step asserts the scale-0 blocked run draws nothing, but PressedArrow is deliberately static (comment in StaticBoardSurface.native.tsx:207-208, 'Static on purpose so it appears on the next frame and never moves') and is unaffected by reduce motion, so a scripted press that outlasts PRESS_PREVIEW_DELAY_MS (64 ms, BoardView.tsx) draws an accent-coloured over-stroke at scale 0 too. [READ] Whether the scale-0 run fails therefore depends on the tap script's hold time, which the step never pins.
kills.replacement: Require a validation pair per phase, not one pair for the tool, and add a motion-specific assertion for `exit`: the gate must compare a mid-phase frame against ANOTHER mid-phase frame at a different offset in the same run and require the dash to have MOVED, not merely changed alpha. Pin the scripted tap's hold time below 64 ms so the press preview is provably absent from the scale-0 control, and state that in the calibration doc.

kills.reason: Right instrument, disclosure text too narrow. The step's documented rule is 'a feedback number measured at scale 0 describes the reduced-motion variant and may not be quoted as the shipped experience.' The `exit` phase is not a feedback number — it is drawn entirely inside the retained native view — and it is equally invalidated, via the reducedMotion field of the exit protocol rather than via Reanimated. [READ nativeExitAnimation.ts serializer + ArrowsBoardView.kt] The step also does not say the app must be relaunched after the setting changes: ReducedMotion.ts captures the value once at JS module init, so a `settings put` against a running process changes nothing. [EXECUTED: cat ReducedMotion.ts]
kills.replacement: Widen `reducedMotionVariantMeasured: true` to fire whenever ANY phase is recorded at scale 0, not only with --feedback, and name the exit phase explicitly in the docs/perf-harness.md rule. Add a hard force-stop-and-relaunch between setting the scale and starting the workload, and record in the JSON whether that relaunch happened. State in the same doc that the exit-phase column of docs/perf-tap-forgiveness-ab-2026-09-08.md and the 2026-09-01 reference both measured the non-moving variant and are not baselines for any scale-1 run.

kills.reason: The instrument as specified cannot be trusted for the phase it will be used on most. It sets transition_animation_scale and animator_duration_scale to 1 and asserts the read-back, but says nothing about WHEN relative to app launch. Reanimated reads the system flag once at JS module init [EXECUTED: ReducedMotion.ts], so setting the scale after the app is already running yields a manifest that says 1 while the process still behaves as reduce-motion — a capture that is silently the wrong variant with a perfectly plausible manifest. That is precisely the class of failure this project has been burned by. Separately, the step's own acceptance concedes it may not be able to photograph a 300 ms effect and defers to the recorder frame rate, which is honest, but every downstream acceptance in W2 is written as 'at least three consecutive frames' without stating the frame rate that makes three frames of 300 ms achievable.
kills.replacement: Require the sequence: set both scales -> force-stop the package -> launch -> read back BOTH the settings and an in-app __DEV__ log of useReducedMotion()'s value -> abort if they disagree. Write the app-reported value into the manifest, not only the device setting. Then measure the recorder's actual achieved frame rate once and publish it, so every downstream 'at least N frames' criterion is expressed against a measured rate rather than an assumed one.

kills.reason: The step's own A/B protocol is self-defeating at the pinned harness. It prescribes `npm run perf:android --level 3827 --runs 10 --feedback`, which runs validateDevice and forces animator_duration_scale to 0 (benchmark.mjs:353) [EXECUTED grep]. The feature under test is a withTiming ramp on the press-preview stroke. At scale 0 that withTiming jumps to its final value on the first frame, so the A/B measures the ramp turned OFF against HEAD's snap — i.e. it measures no difference, by construction, and would report 'no regression' regardless of the ramp's real cost. This is the exact reason the press preview exists in its current form: docs/perf-tap-forgiveness-ab-2026-09-08.md records that drawing the preview at touch-down cost enough to warrant the 64 ms gate, and that measurement is the only stated justification for the snap.
kills.replacement: Do not start this step until W6-11 ships --motion-scale and W2-02/W0-03 give the ramp an explicit ReduceMotion.Never. Then re-specify the A/B at --motion-scale 1, and state up front that there is no comparable HEAD baseline at scale 1 — both arms must be re-measured in the same session. My recommendation is to leave the flag at 0 and not spend the step: the snap is load-bearing and documented, and the only evidence for changing it is taste.

kills.reason: The scrim mechanism is right (a solid-colour sibling quad rather than a container alpha over two overlapping compound paths is the correct call, and the perf reasoning about the offscreen buffer is sound). The sequencing is the problem: loadLevel becomes reachable ONLY from a withTiming completion callback, and the scrim's opacity is the only thing that can reveal the board. Background the app mid-fade on Android and the Choreographer stops feeding frames, so the fade stalls and loadLevel does not run until the app returns. W2-06 — the less dangerous of the two, since a stuck panel still leaves a playable board underneath — explicitly requires a background-during-entrance test; W2-04, which gates the level load itself, requires none. W0-02 exists in this same plan precisely because this codebase already shipped one animation-callback-only state transition with no backstop (SplashScreen.tsx:47-56). Second, unstated cost: the board rebuild under the cover is not free JS. Changing `board` fires BoardView's useLayoutEffect -> new BoardArrowArtCache -> geometryForNativeView() for up to 260 arrows -> visibilityMask -> the native setGeometry, which re-parses the whole string and rebuilds both compound paths under a lock. [READ BoardView.tsx:251-283, arrowGeometry.ts:179-191, ArrowsBoardView.kt setGeometry/rebuildCompoundPathsLocked] The step's 'no gap longer than 3 recorded frames' criterion is measuring exactly that block, which is good, but the criterion was chosen before anyone measured how long the block is.
kills.replacement: Give the transition a deterministic settle in the W0-02 shape: a JS timer plus an AppState-'active' fallback that runs loadLevel and forces the scrim to 0 if the animation has not completed, with a one-shot guard so it cannot run twice. Add 'background the app mid-fade, return, board is loaded and interactive' to the acceptance. Measure the loadLevel block on the densest board FIRST (it is a straight timer around the useLayoutEffect) and set the fade duration from it, rather than asserting 180 ms and then checking the gap.

kills.reason: Two problems. (1) The dense-board acceptance is not a test of amplitude. 'Capture a blocked tap at level 168 and confirm no frame shows the tapped arrow's tail overlapping a neighbour's ink. If it does, the amplitude is too large.' Work the geometry: STROKE is 0.144 cell so the round cap projects 0.072 cell past the tail endpoint (arrowGeometry.ts) [READ]. Against a PERPENDICULAR neighbour whose ink is a 0.144-wide band through the adjacent cell centre, overlap needs a backward excursion above ~0.856 cell — unreachable, so the criterion never fires. Against a COLLINEAR neighbour whose body abuts the tail — common on a mask-packed board, which is what fillMask produces — the inks are already adjacent and ANY non-zero excursion overlaps, so the criterion fires at every amplitude including the smallest. The gate is therefore uninformative in both directions and tells you nothing about the number it is supposed to bound. (2) The step correctly flags that feedbackCurves.test.ts:17's `d >= 0` assertion must be REPLACED not deleted, and correctly requires a bound — but the bound itself ('|min| as a stated fraction of the peak') is never stated, while the peak IS measured (~0.22 cell, from the file's own comment). That is a brief pinning a constraint whose value nobody wrote.
kills.replacement: Replace the overlap gate with a stated amplitude bound in cells, expressed against the measured peak (e.g. |min| <= X * 0.22 cell) and asserted in jest, with X chosen from the same capture the owner picks the feel from. Keep the dense-board capture as a look-at-it check, not as a pass/fail criterion. Note in the step that both renderers read these worklets, so one function body changes Skia and web together — that part of the step's reasoning is correct and verified.

kills.reason: The step's central correction is RIGHT and I verified it: the serializer emits exactly 10 header tokens (id, arrowIndex, durationMs, reducedMotion, trailStrokeWidth, bodyLen, totalLen, dirX, dirY, n) and Kotlin asserts `tokens.size != EXIT_HEADER_TOKEN_COUNT + pointCount*2` with EXIT_HEADER_TOKEN_COUNT=10, so appending a combo field would silently kill every exit. trailStrokeWidth genuinely is per-event and per-slot on both platforms (ArrowsBoardView.kt drawExitSlot `trailPaint.strokeWidth = slot.trailStrokeWidth`; Swift `trail.lineWidth`). [READ] Two things are wrong. (1) The geometric ceiling is derived backwards. The step caps the bead at 2*HEAD_HALF = 0.54 cell 'or the tube will read wider than the head'. But the trail inherits ROUND caps from shaftPaint (`trailPaint = Paint(shaftPaint)`) [READ], so at 0.54 cell the leading cap projects 0.27 cell past the dash end while the head's half-width is also 0.27 — the stated ceiling is the exact point at which the tube swallows the head, not a safe bound below it. (2) The width acceptance is not measurable where it is specified. The difference between 0.26 and 0.54 cell is 4.2 dp vs 8.6 dp at a median 16 dp cell, but level 168 is one of the densest boards and the step names it as the dense-board check — at the ~8.6 dp cells that board reaches at fit-to-view, the two widths are ~2.2 px and ~4.6 px, which is not a reliable pixel measurement off a screenrecord frame. And the capture must run at --motion-scale 1 or the dash will not move at all, which the step does not say.
kills.replacement: Set the ceiling strictly below the head's half-width plus the cap projection — a bead whose outer edge stays inside the arrowhead silhouette, which given ROUND caps means well under 0.54 cell. State the step->width mapping explicitly (it is currently 'a bounded factor of the step' with no factor). Take the width measurement at a stated zoom on a sparse board where the cell is large enough to resolve, and use level 168 only for the does-it-read-as-chunky judgement. Add --motion-scale 1 to the capture command. The wire-format-unchanged and OFF-path-byte-identical criteria are good and should stay.

kills.reason: Mechanically safe — I confirmed the native path has no JS cleanup timer (exitCleanupTimers are used only in the web 'slither' branch; the native slot self-clears when progress >= 1 in drawExitSlot) and the 160..1000 ms parser band is real on both platforms. [READ BoardView.tsx handleTap, ArrowsBoardView.kt] But the step is not independently decidable, and the plan treats it as if it were. F feeds W2-05's won-delay derivation (won delay >= final slither + hold), and W5-06 — in a different workstream — wants to draw a silhouette reveal 'inside that 450 ms' on the same empty board. At F=2.0 the final slither alone is 640 ms, W2-05's derived won delay goes past 800 ms, and W5-06's reveal has no window at all. Three steps, two workstreams, one budget, no arbiter.
kills.replacement: Make F, the empty-board hold, the won delay and the clear reveal ONE owner decision taken from ONE capture, and record the resulting timeline as a single table of derived constants. Do not let W2-05, W2-09 and W5-06 each pick a slice of the same 450 ms in isolation.

kills.reason: The FLAG TEST reasoning is mostly sound and I checked it: at the clear instant the blocker node really is null, because handleTap does `setBlocker(current => current?.arrow === owner ? null : current)` and the blocking arrow must itself have been removed before the board can empty; shaking is either null or the just-removed arrow, which handleTap clears explicitly; pressed is cleared by handlePressEnd. [READ BoardView.tsx handleTap/handlePressEnd] So the fourth Skia slot is genuinely free. What is not sound is the budget: the step spends the same 450 ms window that W2-05 wants to derive and W2-09 wants to lengthen, from a different workstream, and it gives no durations of its own ('fading in and out inside that 450 ms'). It also inherits the reduce-motion trap it half-names: its own acceptance says the silhouette must still appear with reduce motion ON, which means the reveal's driver must not be a bare withTiming — that is the W0-03/W2-02 fix, and this step must be sequenced after it rather than re-deriving it.
kills.replacement: Hold until the single timeline decision from W2-05/W2-09 exists and the reduce-motion policy has shipped, then re-scope with explicit fade-in/hold/fade-out durations that fit inside whatever window that decision leaves. Keep the empty-board pixel-diff guard on the board region — that part is a good check.

kills.reason: It asks for the right three numbers (generation time, payload size, O(n) visibleMask rebuild) but is the ONLY step in the entire plan that measures the mask rebuild, and it sits in W3 — after W0 and W2 have already shipped changes on the blocked-tap path that trigger it twice per event. Also, its exit-phase measurements inherit the reduce-motion branch: run through the standard harness they will measure the stationary dash, so a payload/arrow-count sensitivity result for the exit is not a result about the shipped exit.
kills.replacement: Move the mask-rebuild measurement forward, before W0-03 and W2-07 touch the blocked path, and isolate it: it is a straight timer around the visibilityMask memo plus the native setVisibleMask -> rebuildCompoundPathsLocked round trip, both of which are O(n) with per-element allocation at n up to 250. Run the exit-phase half at --motion-scale 1 once W6-11 exists, and label any exit number taken before that as measuring the non-moving variant.

kills.reason: The step is correct that the value is consumed by the Kotlin paint and that verifying it through the web SVG path would prove nothing — that reasoning is good and I confirmed the mechanism (trailStrokeWidth travels in the payload and lands on trailPaint.strokeWidth per slot). But the prescribed evidence is 'emulator screen recordings via adb screenrecord at each candidate', with no mention of animator_duration_scale. Recorded through the standard harness environment, or on any emulator left at scale 0 by a previous benchmark run, all four candidates render a dash that does not move — so the owner would be picking a trail thickness from four recordings of a stationary bead. It also collides with W2-08, which modulates the same field per combo step; picking a resting value and a combo multiplier independently, in two workstreams, is how you end up with an escalated bead wider than the ceiling W2-08 set.
kills.replacement: Add: set both animation scales to 1, force-stop, relaunch, and log the app's own useReducedMotion() value into the recording's filename before capturing. Sequence W5-12 before W2-08 so the resting value is fixed first and W2-08's escalation factor is chosen against it, not against 0.26.

unmeasured_numbers: W2-04: the 180 ms cross-fade. Sourced to DESIGN.md's own 160-220 band and to App.tsx:63's existing FadeIn, which is a citation, not a measurement — and critically it was chosen BEFORE anyone measured the synchronous loadLevel block it has to cover (new BoardArrowArtCache + geometryForNativeView for up to 260 arrows + visibilityMask + native re-parse and compound-path rebuild). The step's own 'no gap longer than 3 recorded frames' criterion is a test of a number that has never been measured.

W2-08: the step->trailStrokeWidth mapping. Specified only as 'a bounded factor of the step'. The factor itself is absent; only the ceiling (0.54 cell) is given, and that ceiling is mis-derived — with ROUND caps inherited from shaftPaint the bead's cap projects half its width past the dash end, so 0.54 cell is exactly where the tube reaches the arrowhead's half-width, not safely below it.

W2-07: the anticipation amplitude bound. Stated as '|min| as a stated fraction of the peak' with the fraction never stated. The peak IS measured (~0.22 cell, from feedbackCurves.ts's own comment), so the missing number is one ratio — but it is the only number in the step that decides whether the effect is visible or invisible.

W2-09: F in {1.0, 1.5, 2.0}. Correctly flagged as owner-picked from a capture, but the candidate SET is invented, and F=2.0 x EXIT_TRAIL_MAX_DURATION_MS(320) = 640 ms already exceeds W2-05's current 450 ms won delay, so one of the three candidates is knowably incompatible with a sibling step before the capture is even taken.

W2-05: the 'deliberate hold on the empty board'. The step notes 450-320 = 130 ms of hold exists today (arithmetic, correct) but never says how long a hold needs to be to read as a hold, and then W5-06 proposes drawing a whole reveal inside it.

W5-12: EXIT_TRAIL_STROKE_CELLS candidates {0.144, 0.18, 0.22, 0.26}. Explicitly labelled a sampling grid, which is the honest handling — but the grid's spacing was picked, not derived, and the step gives no guidance on what resolves at the 8.6 dp median cell it will be judged at.
W2-12: PRESS_PREVIEW_RAMP_MS. Default 0 (today's snap); the ON value is never given, and the A/B that was supposed to justify it cannot measure it at the harness's forced scale 0.

W2-01: the recorder frame rate. Every downstream acceptance in W2 is written as 'at least three consecutive frames' of effects lasting 300-650 ms, but nobody has measured what frame rate adb screenrecord actually achieves on this software-GPU emulator. W2-01's own acceptance is honest about this ('if it cannot, the recorder frame rate is too low and the step is not done'); the eight steps that depend on it are not.

W6-12: the pixel-diff floor. Correctly deferred to a three-set calibration with a stated kill condition — this is the one number in the plan handled the way the harness demands, and it should be the template for the others.

W3-04: A_end is pinned at 249 arrows because that is the measured v1 maximum, i.e. 'the highest arrow count the retained native board view has ever been measured at'. That is a real bound and correctly cited — but the measurement it rests on is the exit/blocked phase numbers from an emulator running the reduce-motion variant, so the ceiling is honest about its provenance and dishonest about what that provenance measured.
sequencing_errors: W0-03 and W2-02 are the same edit to the same six withTiming sites, in two workstreams, with different scopes (6 sites vs 27 + a lint rule) and mutually invalidating acceptance. Both use 'on HEAD the same capture contains zero such frames' as their pre-fix anchor; whichever ships second cannot produce that anchor. Merge them and ship the reduce-motion policy once.

W6-11 (--motion-scale) is a hard prerequisite for W2-12's A/B, for W5-12's candidate recordings, for W2-08's and W2-09's exit captures, and for W3-09's exit numbers — but W6 is the second-to-last workstream. Every motion and exit measurement in W2, W3 and W5 is specified against an instrument that only W6 repairs. W6-11 is an S-sized change to one script; move it to W0.

W2-01 (the capture instrument) is declared the prerequisite for W2-02..W2-12, but W0-03 — a motion change to the same three effects — ships first in W0 and closes on hand-run screenrecord. Either W2-01 moves ahead of W0-03 or W0-03's manual capture is the accepted evidence and W2-01 is being built to re-verify something already shipped. Pick one.

W6-12/W6-13 (pixel floor + effect-rendered gate) are positioned as the guard that stops a number being quoted for an effect that never drew — but W2 ships eight new visual effects before W6 exists, so the guard arrives after everything it was built to guard.

W2-05, W2-09 and W5-06 each claim a slice of the same post-clear window (450 ms today) from two different workstreams, with W2-05 explicitly deriving its delay from W2-09's unpicked F and W5-06 assuming 450 ms is still available. No step owns the timeline.

W2-08 (combo escalation of trailStrokeWidth) and W5-12 (resting trailStrokeWidth) modulate the same payload field from two workstreams. W5-12 must fix the resting value first, or W2-08's escalation factor and its 0.54 cell ceiling are computed against a number W5 is about to change.

W3-09 is the only step that measures the O(n) visibleMask rebuild, and it sits behind the entire W3 curve work — while W0-03, W2-07 and W6-02 all ship changes on the blocked-tap path, which is the path that triggers that rebuild twice per event.
missing_work: NOBODY MEASURES THE MASK REBUILD, WHICH IS THE LARGEST PER-EVENT COST IN THE ARCHITECTURE. Every blocked tap adds and then removes the tapped arrow from excludedArrows (BoardView.tsx: `if (shaking) excluded.add(shaking.arrow)`), which invalidates the nativeVisibilityMask memo twice. Each rebuild is `new Set(visibleArrows)` plus `orderedArrows.map(...).join('')` — two O(n) passes with n string allocations at n up to 250 (arrowGeometry.ts:183-191) — and each result is pushed through setVisibleMask into rebuildCompoundPathsLocked, which re-adds up to 250 Paths into two compound Paths under a lock (ArrowsBoardView.kt). That is four O(n) passes and two full compound-path rebuilds per blocked tap, and it is the reason `blocked` is the worst phase in the 2026-09-08 table (35.7-55.1 ms p95 across five samples). Not one step in W0-W8 isolates it. [READ + EXECUTED grep]

NO STEP RECORDS OR SIGNS OFF WHAT THE EXIT LOOKS LIKE UNDER REDUCE MOTION. The shipped behaviour — dash frozen in place, head does not translate, linear alpha fade over the same duration — is a deliberate-looking branch in both Kotlin and Swift that appears in no design document, no acceptance criterion and no escalation. It is probably the right degradation, but it is currently a fact discovered by reading the renderer rather than a decision.

NO STEP RECONCILES THE HISTORICAL EXIT-PHASE NUMBERS. docs/perf-tap-forgiveness-ab-2026-09-08.md and the 2026-09-01 reference both carry an `exit` column taken at animator_duration_scale 0, i.e. of the non-moving variant.
